dossier.candidate: Reselling / flipping / arbitrage (FB Marketplace and Kijiji flipping, liquidation pallets, retail and online arbitrage to Amazon.ca, eBay), plus whether the owner's Canadian tool price scraper can support tool flipping
dossier.summary:
RESEARCH LIMITATION (read first): the network proxy blocked WebFetch and curl for every domain I tried: sell.amazon.ca, sellercentral.amazon.ca, canada.ca, ebay.ca, bstock.com, cbc.ca, reddit, moosemoney.com, ecomcalctools.com, liquidationprime.ca, directliquidation.com and homedepot.ca. The session's web-search budget ran out after 12 successful searches. So every fact below comes from search-result titles and snippets, not from full pages I opened. The eBay.ca fee schedule, B-Stock Canada buyer terms, Amazon.ca per-item Individual fee, Amazon.ca FBA fee tables in CAD, and Reddit failure threads could not be retrieved and are marked "not found".

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS: Flipping on FB Marketplace and Kijiji is the fastest way to get first cash, probably within days. It needs very little setup, and the AI can do listing copy and price tracking. But the best documented Canadian-style anecdote I found is about $2,333/month profit (ESTIMATE: $35,000 over 15 months). That is less than half the $5,000 target, and it is labour-heavy: messaging, pickups, meetups, and usually a vehicle. Amazon.ca arbitrage costs CAD $29.99/month (Professional plan) plus a 15% referral fee in Tools and Home Improvement (CAD $0.40 minimum) plus FBA fees with a 3.5% fuel surcharge since 17 April 2026. The most obvious tool brands for flipping (DeWalt, Milwaukee) are brand-gated. One Amazon.ca seller-forum thread reports failing to get DeWalt-ungated after 5 months. Liquidation pallets are available in the GTA (B-Stock lists Amazon Canada and Best Buy Canada as sellers, Liquidation Prime has $1 starting bids, and Mississauga warehouses exist). But reviews say pallets can hold "only a handful of valuable items", and CBC reported returned Amazon goods in Toronto liquidation stores still carrying buyers' personal information.

TAX: sales platforms report sellers to CRA once they pass 30 sales or about CAD $2,800 a year (rules effective 2024). GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once taxable revenue passes $30,000 in four consecutive quarters. At the revenue needed to net $5k/month on Amazon, that happens within about 2 months.

THE OWNER'S SCRAPER: all 54 cached queries show priceCount 0. Every entry is a "checkManually" search link with price 0. In its current form it cannot support tool arbitrage.

VERDICT: good as a fast, low-setup way to bridge income in weeks 1–4. It is unlikely to reliably average CAD $5,000/month net within 60 days without a vehicle, several thousand dollars of working capital, and near full-time physical effort.
dossier.time_to_first_revenue: FB Marketplace and Kijiji local flipping: probably days, but no official source measures this. The anecdotal basis is MooseMoney's article "I Spent 20 Hours Hustling on Facebook Marketplace to Figure Out What Are The Best Items To Flip in Canada" (https://www.moosemoney.com/best-items-to-flip-on-marketplace/, title and snippet only). It reports that consoles, keyboards and controllers "move fast when priced right". Cash is usually paid in person at pickup, so money arrives the same day, but I have no source for that; it is an unverified assumption. Amazon.ca (FBA or merchant-fulfilled): account-verification time, FBA inbound check-in time and payout schedule were all not found (sell.amazon.ca and sellercentral.amazon.ca were blocked). The one relevant source says capital is "locked up longer due to shipping time, customs, and FBA intake" for cross-border arbitrage (https://arbitragecyclops.com/blog/cross-border-arbitrage-canada-us/, an industry vendor). Liquidation pallets: auction close plus pickup plus sorting plus individual resale. No time estimate was found. Liquidation Prime lists pallets with starting bids at $1 (https://liquidationprime.ca/, snippet). Overall ESTIMATE, not sourced: first dollar within 3–10 days via local flipping; first Amazon payout likely several weeks out (no source found).

dossier.path_to_5k_math:
All numbers below are ESTIMATES. The only sourced inputs are the fees and the one anecdote. Per-flip profit and margins are HYPOTHETICAL because no sourced average was found.

(A) Local flipping on FB Marketplace and Kijiji. Best sourced anecdote: ESTIMATE $35,000 / 15 months = $2,333/month. Reaching $5,000 needs ESTIMATE 5,000 / 2,333 = 2.14x that person's average.
- At a HYPOTHETICAL $60 average net profit per flip: ESTIMATE 5,000 / 60 = 84 flips/month, which is 84 / 30 = 2.8 sales/day and about 168 buy-plus-sell meetups/month.
- At a HYPOTHETICAL $150/flip (furniture or tool lots, needs a vehicle): ESTIMATE 5,000 / 150 = 34 flips/month.
- Working capital at a HYPOTHETICAL $100 average buy cost and 2-week turnover: ESTIMATE 84 x 100 / 2 = $4,200.

(B) Amazon.ca online arbitrage in Tools (15% referral, $29.99/month plan). At a HYPOTHETICAL 20% net margin after all fees, required revenue is ESTIMATE (5,000 + 29.99) / 0.20 = $25,150/month.
- Referral fees on that revenue: ESTIMATE 0.15 x 25,150 = $3,773.
- If FBA, prep and inbound shipping cost a HYPOTHETICAL 15% more (about $3,773), cost of goods is about ESTIMATE 25,150 - 3,773 - 3,773 - 5,030 = $12,574/month.
- At a HYPOTHETICAL 6-week cash cycle, capital tied up is about ESTIMATE 12,574 x 1.5 = $18,860.
- GST/HST: ESTIMATE 30,000 / 25,150 = 1.19 months of sales passes the $30,000 small-supplier threshold, so registration is required in month 2.

(C) Pallets at the $200–$800 snippet range. With a HYPOTHETICAL 2x gross resale recovery on a $500 pallet, profit is $500 before transport, fees, unsellable items and labour. So 5,000 / 500 = 10 pallets/month = $5,000/month buy-in, and hundreds of individual items to test, photograph, list and sell.

Conclusion (ESTIMATE): each path needs roughly $4k–$19k of working capital and/or 80+ transactions a month, with no sourced evidence that a beginner reaches that within 60 days.
dossier.startup_cost_cad:
ESTIMATE, varies by path:
- Local flipping: $0 platform fees for FB Marketplace and Kijiji basic listings (fee terms not verified; not found), plus inventory of $300–$4,200 (HYPOTHETICAL, see math), plus a vehicle for anything bulky (owner's own or rental; cost not found).
- Amazon.ca arbitrage: $29.99/month Professional plan (sourced), plus inventory of roughly $5k–$19k to reach $5k/month net (HYPOTHETICAL), plus scanning/repricing software (price not found), plus prep and shipping (not found).
- Pallets: $1 starting bids up to $200–$800+ per pallet (snippets), plus buyer premium and freight (not found), plus storage space.
Realistic minimum to start testing: ESTIMATE about $500–$1,000 for local flipping only.
requirements: Capital: working inventory money. ESTIMATE $500 minimum for local flipping; ESTIMATE $4k–$19k to reach $5k/month net (see math). Savings unknown, so this is a gating question for the owner.

Vehicle: effectively required for furniture, large tools, pallets and warehouse pickups (Mississauga liquidation warehouses and B-Stock/Liquidation Prime pickups). Small electronics and hand tools can be done by transit at lower volume.
Storage space: a garage, basement or locker for inventory and pallets. Condo/apartment rules may prohibit it (not researched).
Physical labour: lifting furniture and pallets, repeated meetups, testing and cleaning items.

English level: functional conversational English for negotiation and messaging on FB Marketplace and Kijiji. Korean-language community boards could supplement this (not researched). Amazon Seller Central is in English and French (not verified).

Amazon.ca path: government ID, bank account and credit card for Seller Central identity verification; Professional plan at $29.99/month; ungating invoices from authorized distributors for brands like DeWalt and Milwaukee (retail receipts are generally not accepted per ungating guides — see brand-gating sources).
SIN and tax records: platforms report sellers passing 30 sales or about $2,800/year to CRA; business income is reported on T2125 (per the northos.ca T2125 guide title).
Smartphone with camera and data for listings, comps and meetups.
Time: 40+ hours/week to approach the transaction volumes in the math.

regulations.fact: Reporting Rules for Digital Platform Operators (Part XX of the Income Tax Act, via Bill C-47, Royal Assent June 22, 2023) have applied since January 1, 2024. Platforms collect seller name, address, TIN and total sales proceeds and report them to CRA. The first reports were due January 31, 2025.

eBay.ca: Canadian residents who sell over $2,800 (USD $2,044) or pass 30 sales transactions in a calendar year have their information reported to CRA. Failing to provide requested information may result in a $500 CRA fine (search-summary wording; exact source sentence not opened).

A third-party search summary states Facebook Marketplace and Kijiji also report under these rules. This is not confirmed on an official Meta or Kijiji page (not found), especially for cash local-pickup sales.

GST/HST small supplier: $30,000 or less in worldwide taxable revenues over the last four consecutive calendar quarters. If $30,000 is passed in a single quarter, registration takes effect no later than the day of the supply that crossed it, and GST/HST must be charged on that supply. If it is passed over four quarters, the business stops being a small supplier at the end of the month after that quarter. Voluntary registration is allowed.
CRA audit attention on online sellers (Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, eBay), per the tax-law firm article title 'CRA Targets Online Sellers ... Audits, Tax Risks' (title and snippet only).

Amazon brand gating: restricted brands such as DeWalt and Milwaukee need approval through Seller Central, typically with invoices from the manufacturer or an authorized wholesaler, or a brand authorization letter.

Quebec QST, BC PST, Alberta rules, and municipal second-hand-goods licensing (Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Ottawa, Montreal): not found in this research. The owner must verify with the province and city before buying and reselling at volume.

Product-safety and recall rules for reselling used or returned goods (e.g., Canada Consumer Product Safety Act): not verified in this research because egress was blocked. Owner should check Health Canada recall listings before reselling returns.

ai_can_build: A comp and deal-evaluation spreadsheet or web tool: buy price, sold-comps range, Amazon.ca referral (15% tools, $0.40 minimum), FBA fee input, 3.5% surcharge, GST/HST flag at $30k, and profit/ROI per item
Listing-copy generator templates for FB Marketplace and Kijiji (English, and Korean for Korean community boards), with title, description, condition checklist and pricing tiers
Negotiation and reply message templates plus a scam-screening checklist. The human sends them, because the AI cannot post from the owner's accounts

An inventory and cash-flow tracker: items, cost, list date, sold price, days-to-sell, and running totals of sales count and dollars against the CRA 30-sale and $2,800 platform threshold and the $30k GST/HST threshold
T2125-ready bookkeeping export: income, cost of goods, fees and mileage categories
Repurpose the existing Next.js repo into a private 'flip calculator' and inventory dashboard, replacing the broken scraper with manual price entry and saved retailer clearance links
Google Calendar blocks for pickup and meetup routes and auction close times; Gmail filters and labels for B-Stock and Liquidation Prime notifications
Research checklists for unknowns: municipal licensing, provincial sales tax, B-Stock buyer requirements
human_must_do: Decide how much capital to risk, and provide the vehicle and storage (or rent them)
Open and verify accounts with ID: Amazon Seller Central, eBay, B-Stock, Liquidation Prime; pay fees; hold bank accounts
Source inventory in person: curb finds, garage sales, retail clearance aisles, liquidation warehouses and auction pickups
Post listings and reply to buyers from their own FB Marketplace and Kijiji accounts. The AI cannot post to the owner's accounts
Meet buyers and sellers, inspect and test items, handle cash or e-transfers safely
Lift, clean, repair, photograph, pack and ship items; drop off at carriers or prepare FBA shipments
Apply for Amazon brand and category ungating with qualifying distributor invoices
Register for GST/HST when required, file taxes, and keep receipts
Wipe or destroy any customer personal data found in returned-goods pallets (see the CBC report)
dossier.seasonality: Amazon applies holiday peak FBA fees in Canada (about CAD $0.39/unit on average, https://amzprep.com/holiday-peak-fulfillment-fees/), so Amazon treats Q4 as a peak period. Starting in October 2026 means entering Q4 with higher fulfilment costs; exact 2026 peak dates were not found. Holiday demand for consoles, electronics and tools as gifts is plausible but not sourced here. Seasonal effects on FB Marketplace and Kijiji (for example, fewer furniture pickups in winter, or lawn tools selling in spring and snow equipment in fall) were not found in any source; they are unverified assumptions only.
risks: Income shortfall: the best-sourced flipper anecdote works out to about $2,333/month (ESTIMATE), under half the $5,000 target
Inventory risk: unsold, broken or missing-part items. Liquidation-pallet reviews mention 'only a handful of valuable items'
Capital lock-up: Amazon FBA and cross-border arbitrage tie up money in transit and intake, which clashes with a 30-day cash need

Amazon account risk: brand gating (DeWalt and Milwaukee are restricted, with a Canadian seller reporting 5 months of failed DeWalt ungating); suspension risk from IP or authenticity complaints on retail-sourced goods
Fee creep: 3.5% FBA fuel surcharge since April 17, 2026; peak fees; Device Accessories referral up to 45%
Privacy and legal exposure: returned-goods pallets in Toronto were found to contain buyers' personal information (CBC)
Personal safety and scam risk at in-person meetups and with online payment scams (no Canadian scam statistics retrieved; not found)
Tax: CRA platform reporting past 30 sales or $2,800 means the income will be visible to CRA; at volume, mandatory GST/HST registration after $30,000
Saturation: many paid 'how to flip' guides on Gumroad target beginners. This is an observation from search results that the niche is heavily marketed, not a measured saturation statistic
Physical and vehicle dependency: without a vehicle, only small items at lower volume
Scraper dependency: the owner's price-comparison repo currently produces zero prices, so it gives no deal-finding edge

counter_evidence.fact: The owner's own scraper: public/cache/index.json has 54 tracked queries and 0 with any price (priceCount 0 for all, checked 2026-09-23). Each store entry is a search link with price 0 and checkManually true, and daily GitHub Actions commits keep producing empty data. Scripts use plain fetch() with a browser User-Agent against walmart.ca, homedepot.ca, rona.ca and others, which are evidently blocked. Local repo evidence, not a web page.

An Amazon.ca Seller Central forum thread, 'Dewalt Brand Ungate in CANADA': a seller reports repeated ungating applications over about five months with no approval and no clear rejection reason. DeWalt is one of the main tool-flip brands.

CBC News: products returned to Amazon were found at Toronto liquidation stores along with buyers' personal information. Amazon's liquidator contracts require removing personal info, but it still happened. Article date not visible in the snippet.
Liquidation-pallet reviews are mixed; some buyers report 'only a handful of valuable items' in pallets (search summary of review pages).

Marketplace flipping 'is not passive income, as messaging alone can take hours'; beginners should expect 3–5 months of disciplined work (community newsletter). That conflicts with a 30-day income deadline.
Cross-border arbitrage adds customs, logistics and multi-currency complexity, and money stays locked up longer. The vendor itself advises starting small and scaling gradually.
Many results for 'Facebook Marketplace flipping' are paid Gumroad courses (momhustleclub, daddysidehustle, chicacademy). Earnings claims in this niche are often self-promotional and unverified.
Specific Reddit failure stories (r/Flipping, r/FulfillmentByAmazon, r/PersonalFinanceCanada): not found. Reddit was blocked and no Reddit threads came up in the searches.

dossier.score_rationale:
Speed 7: local FB Marketplace and Kijiji flipping needs no approvals and pays cash at pickup, so the first sale can plausibly come within days (anecdotal, MooseMoney). The Amazon and pallet paths are slower.

Probability of $5k within 60 days is 2 for three reasons:
- The only quantified anecdote is about $2,333/month (ESTIMATE).
- Reaching $5k needs about 84 flips/month at a hypothetical $60/flip, or about $25k/month Amazon revenue with about $19k tied up (ESTIMATE).
- No source shows beginners reaching this within 60 days; the one community source says expect 3–5 months.

Capital-light 4: local flipping can start with a few hundred dollars, but scaling to $5k net needs roughly $4k–$19k of working capital, often plus a vehicle and storage.

AI leverage 3: the AI can build calculators, listing copy, trackers and bookkeeping. The revenue-generating work — sourcing, negotiating from the owner's accounts, pickups, testing, lifting, shipping and ungating — is human and physical.

Low-risk 4: the risks are dead inventory, pallet duds, Amazon gating and suspension, the FBA surcharge and peak fees, meetup safety and scams, personal-data exposure in returns, and CRA platform reporting plus GST/HST. There are no licensing barriers found, and a cautious small-scale start keeps the downside limited.

Scraper: it currently returns 0 prices for all 54 queries. Retailers block plain-fetch scraping, and DeWalt and Milwaukee are gated on Amazon. So the existing repo realistically cannot support tool-flipping arbitrage within 30 days. It is better repurposed as a manual-entry profit calculator and inventory tracker.

hidden_costs_or_blockers: EI interaction (missing from the dossier; not verified this session): the owner is losing a job next week and may apply for Employment Insurance. Self-employment or flipping income usually has to be declared on EI reports and may reduce or disqualify benefits if the self-employment is judged full-time. The owner must check the EI self-employment rules on canada.ca before scaling, because this could cost more than the flipping earns.

Evidence quality: the whole dossier rests on search snippets. None of the core Amazon.ca fee figures (plan fee, 15% referral, $0.40 minimum, FBA table, 3.5% surcharge, peak fee) was confirmed on a primary page, in the dossier or in this re-check. Any calculator the AI builds must leave these as editable inputs, not hard-coded 'facts'.
The dossier's 'no 2026 fee increase' statement conflicts with the 3.5% FBA surcharge it also reports. The Amazon math may understate fees.

Amazon retail-arbitrage authenticity risk: retail receipts are generally not accepted for ungating, per the dossier's own sources. The same weakness exposes retail-sourced tool listings to authenticity complaints and account suspension, which can freeze the payout balance. Payout timing and hold periods remain not found.
Amazon seller identity verification time: not found. It could consume a large part of the 30-day window before a single sale.

Local cash sales: the dossier assumes FB Marketplace and Kijiji report to CRA, but this is unverified. Either way, income is taxable. Records must be kept for T2125, including mileage and vehicle costs, which the dossier never costs out.

Vehicle cost (fuel, insurance, wear) is not quantified anywhere, yet it is required for the furniture, pallet and warehouse paths. The pallet path also needs storage space, and condo or lease rules were not researched.

Municipal licensing for second-hand goods dealing in Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Ottawa and Montreal: not found. Volume reselling from home could trigger licence or zoning issues, so check before scaling.
